definition: A system design in which ongoing human feedback (ratings, corrections, preferences) is continually collected and used to improve a deployed AI system over time.
details: Human feedback loops are used both during model training (as in RLHF) and in production systems, where user interactions and corrections can inform future model updates or fine-tuning.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. Think of it this way: A system design in which ongoing human feedback (ratings, corrections, preferences) is continually collected and used to improve a deployed AI system over time. And here is the clever part: Human feedback loops are used both during model training (as in RLHF) and in production systems, where user interactions and corrections can inform future model updates or fine-tuning. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Human Feedback Loop — is what makes everything else possible.
